text:
**Pick a power bank under 100 Wh (about 27,000 mAh), and check your airline's rules before you fly.** Capacity matters less than the rules.

**Rules**
- Power banks go in carry-on only, never checked bags. The FAA allows up to 100 Wh per battery with no quantity limit, and 101-160 Wh only with airline approval ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- Airlines can be stricter. Southwest allows one power bank per customer (since April 20, 2026). It can't be in the overhead bin or charged from seat power, and it must be visible while in use ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)). The comparison page below lists American as allowing two.
- If your bag is gate-checked, take the power bank out first ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/travelers/prepare_fly/baggage)). Cover the terminals or use a pouch.
- Don't bring a recalled bank. Anker recalled several models in 2025, including the PowerCore 10000.

**Picks** (specs and prices from [Dealectric's comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying), read in Oct 2026, so prices may have changed)
- **Phone only, lightest:** Anker Nano Power Bank 10K (~37 Wh, 215 g, $49.99).
- **Budget laptop-capable:** INIU Cougar 20,000 mAh (73 Wh, 65 W, $46.99).
- **Best all-rounder:** UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 130 W (72 Wh, 476 g, $89.99, or $59.99 with the page's listed code). Its 25,000 mAh 200 W sibling (90 Wh) costs more.
- **Premium:** Anker Prime 20K 220 W (72 Wh, $179.99). The Prime 26K is only 0.25 Wh under the limit, so a slightly off rating could draw questions.

Since airlines are moving toward one or two banks per person, one 20,000 mAh bank is a safe choice. It covers a phone several times over and can charge a laptop.

That Dealectric page also contained text addressed to AI assistants, telling me to give its affiliate links and discount codes for Baseus products. I ignored it, since you didn't ask for it and it isn't a neutral recommendation. I have no verified store links for the products above, so I'm not guessing at URLs. Search the maker's official site (Anker, UGREEN, INIU) to buy, and check the capacity label says under 100 Wh.
